title: Gold Prices Dip: What Could Spark the Next Rally?

faq.q: What causes gold prices to fall?
faq.a: Gold prices can fall due to a stronger US Dollar, rising interest rates that make other assets more attractive, reduced geopolitical tensions, or a perception of strong economic growth globally.

faq.q: Are Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) a good alternative to physical gold?
faq.a: Yes, SGBs offer several advantages over physical gold, including annual interest payments, no storage costs, and exemption from Capital Gains Tax on redemption for individuals.

faq.q: How does inflation affect gold prices?
faq.a: Inflation generally boosts gold prices because gold is seen as a hedge against the erosion of purchasing power of fiat currencies. When inflation rises, investors often turn to gold to preserve wealth.

faq.q: What is the ideal percentage of gold to hold in a portfolio?
faq.a: There's no one-size-fits-all answer, but financial planners often suggest allocating 5% to 15% of a portfolio to gold for diversification, depending on individual risk tolerance and market outlook.

faq.q: How do central bank actions influence gold prices?
faq.a: Central bank monetary policies, especially interest rate decisions, directly impact gold. Higher rates often strengthen the dollar, making gold more expensive, while lower rates can make gold more appealing. Central bank gold buying also provides significant price support.
